baseline.name: Array queue with shift-on-pop
baseline.approach: Keep queue order in an array and shift every remaining value after removing the front.
baseline.time: O(1) push and O(q) pop at queue length q

archived.name: Lazy two-stack queue
archived.time: Amortized O(1) push/pop/peek; an individual transfer is O(q)

why: Each value moves to the output stack at most once instead of being shifted after every earlier removal.
quantitative_comparison: Popping q queued items can shift q(q-1)/2 values in the baseline. The archived transfer moves each of those q values between stacks once, followed by q output pops; these operation counts are not an elapsed ratio.
tradeoffs: Worst-case latency for one operation is still linear. Fixed capacity, nonempty pop/peek calls and successful construction are assumed; it is not an unbounded queue.
evidence_basis: Static amortized movement comparison under the same bounded queue workload; no timing benchmark.
